title: Blackcurrant and cream tart
subtitle: a blind-baked pastry shell filled with lightly sweetened cream and poached blackcurrants
excerpt: Blackcurrant and cream tart has a crisp pastry base filled with a sweet cream set with a little gelatine or cornflour, and topped with poached blackcurrants. The cream filling is made separately, poured into the cooled shell, and chilled until set. The sharpness of the blackcurrants balances the richness of the cream.
sourceNotes: Blackcurrants combined with cream-based fillings appear in British pudding and tart traditions from at least the Victorian era. Blackcurrants were a commercially significant British crop through the twentieth century, partly due to their use in Ribena cordial, developed in the 1940s.

glossaryTerms.definition: Baking a pastry shell without filling, using baking paper and beans to keep the base flat and the sides upright.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pastry case can be made the day before. Assemble up to 4 hours ahead of serving and refrigerate.

content.text: Blackcurrant and cream tart is a

pastry case filled with a set cream and topped with poached blackcurrants. The cream sets in the fridge without going into the oven, so the pastry cooks first and the filling goes in once it is cool. The combination of a buttery, crisp base with sharp blackcurrants and sweet cream is a classic summer dessert.

Make the pastry: rub the cold butter into the flour and icing sugar until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Mix in the egg yolk and enough cold water to bring the dough together. Press into a flat disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Roll the pastry to about 3 mm on a lightly floured surface. Line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Trim, then chill for 15 minutes.

Heat the oven to 200 degrees C (fan 180 degrees C / gas 6). Blind bake the pastry with baking paper and beans for 15 minutes, then remove the beans and paper and bake for 8 to 10 minutes more until the base is pale golden and dry. Cool completely.

Poach the blackcurrants: put the blackcurrants, caster sugar, and water in a small saucepan. Heat over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then simmer for 5 minutes until the currants have softened but still hold their shape. Drain, reserving the syrup. Leave to cool.
Whip the double cream with the icing sugar and vanilla until it holds soft, billowy peaks. Spoon into the cooled pastry case and spread level.
Spoon the cooled blackcurrants over the cream. Drizzle with a little of the reserved syrup. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving. Cut straight from the tin.

attrs.problem: Cream filling collapsing and going liquid under the fruit
attrs.avoid: Avoid under-whipped cream or adding the fruit while it is still warm; both cause the cream to break.
attrs.fix: Whip the cream to firm soft peaks, not stiff. Make sure the poached currants and their syrup are completely cold before spooning them onto the cream.

attrs.problem: Pastry base going soft after filling
attrs.avoid: Avoid adding the cream before the pastry shell has cooled completely; steam softens the base.
attrs.fix: The pastry case must be at room temperature before filling. A thin smear of melted white chocolate brushed over the inside base also helps seal it against moisture.
